headline: Democrats' midterm win, Nvidia's CEO exit and Iran tensions mark the week
summary: Democrats locked in control of Congress, capped by Scott Colom's upset Senate win in Mississippi, and Nvidia's Jensen Huang resigned after a week of turmoil. Oil slid on hopes of an Iran deal before Israel reportedly ordered strike readiness and Trump said no deal was needed. At home, Ottawa's $62.3-billion-deficit budget drew continued reaction, Stellantis sold its Brampton plant and Ontario appointed powerful new regional chairs.

top.headline: Democrats take Congress; Colom flips Mississippi Senate seat
top.what: Democrats won both chambers on Nov. 3, and on Wednesday Scott Colom was projected the winner in Mississippi as Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith conceded; Alaska's Senate race is the last one uncalled.
top.why: A Democratic Congress can investigate the administration and contest tariffs starting in January.

top.headline: Oil slides on Iran deal hopes, then Trump says no deal is needed
top.what: Brent crude briefly fell below US$90, its lowest since August, as Trump held off on new strikes; then Israel's cabinet reportedly ordered readiness for an attack and Trump said Thursday the U.S. does not need a deal with Iran.
top.why: Oil prices drive GTA gas prices, inflation and the Bank of Canada's next rate move.

top.headline: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigns after board probe
top.what: Nvidia's board opened an independent investigation on Nov. 8, and on Thursday Huang resigned from all roles; finance chief Colette Kress is interim CEO and the stock opened about 14% lower before paring losses.
top.why: Nvidia is one of the largest holdings in U.S. index funds, so its swings reach Canadian pensions and retirement accounts.

top.headline: Carney government's second budget projects a $62.3B deficit
top.what: Reaction continued to Finance Minister Champagne's Nov. 5 budget, which projects a $62.3-billion deficit for 2026-27 and about $142 billion in new spending over five years.
top.why: It sets federal taxes, spending and borrowing while tariffs and higher interest rates squeeze households.

top.headline: Stellantis sells idled Brampton plant to defence firm Roshel
top.what: Stellantis said Monday it will sell the Brampton assembly plant; Carney called it a betrayal of workers, and federal and Ontario ministers met the company and Unifor in Toronto on Thursday.
top.why: Thousands of Peel Region auto jobs and $529 million in pledged federal support are at stake.

top.headline: Russia and Ukraine agree to large prisoner swap; U.S. envoys meet Putin
top.what: Abu Dhabi talks produced agreement in principle on a large prisoner exchange but no movement on territory; U.S. envoys met Putin in Moscow on Thursday as about 50 leaders gathered in Dublin.
top.why: Any deal or breakdown shapes European security and Canada's allied commitments.

top.headline: Ontario names eight regional chairs with 'strong chair' powers
top.what: The province appointed the heads of Durham, Halton, Muskoka, Niagara, Peel, Waterloo, York and Simcoe, drawing conflict-of-interest complaints over Steven Del Duca in York.
top.why: Appointed chairs now steer regional budgets that drive property taxes, housing approvals and services.

top.headline: Hegseth impeachment shelved 211-204; Jim Jordan to lead House GOP
top.what: Eleven absent Democrats let Republicans send impeachment articles against the defence secretary to committee, and House Republicans picked Jim Jordan over Steve Scalise as their next leader.
top.why: It previews a combative divided Washington when Democrats take the House in January.
